old: “Where has divine love not yet descended into the wound?”
new: Are you asking “Where is that divine love that is not descending upon me to heal my pain?”

old: A genuine opening can show you a depth of love or freedom you hadn’t known was possible. Let that matter without demanding the child receive it on command. Prayer can also evoke abandonment or condemnation, or a teacher’s betrayal can damage something sacred. Ask what was lost and what needs questioning; more of the same practice isn’t automatically the answer.
new: Maybe you had a profound opening that showed you how much more love and freedom is possible. Maybe when you prayed it seemed like you were being abandoned and condemned. Maybe you felt betrayed by a spiritual teacher. It may be worth exploring these, but you might not want to do more of the same.

old: Sometimes practical care helps while the available horizon of life still feels too small. Curiosity about deeper happiness is worth following without pretending to believe an explanation. Other people already have enough love and meaning for the life they want. Spirituality doesn’t need to become another assignment.
new: Sometimes it’s best to get some practical help, and let yourself be curious about finding more happiness, without necessarily believing the explanation of how it’s going to work. Sometimes people have enough love and meaning to just live their lives, and trying to be spiritual is not in their cards.

old: A real wound and a checking loop can coexist. Ask whether this round helps you feel, understand, decide, or respond differently—or whether you’re checking the same question for reassurance. Grief and practice can revisit familiar ground; novelty isn’t required every time.
new: You may have a real wound that needs to be dealt with, but it’s possible you’re caught in a checking loop. Consider asking yourself “Will processing this again actually help me feel, understand, decide, or do something differently? Or is this a form of checking to see if I can get the reassurance that something is finally okay?” Sometimes, whether you’re grieving or doing spiritual practice, it’s okay to cover the same ground again and again.

old: When it is a checking loop, let the thought remain without arguing with it or chasing it away, and return to a chosen activity or relationship. You don’t have to hold an inner meeting every time a thought appears or complete a ritual before you’re allowed to live.
new: But if you think you’re in a checking loop, let the thought be there without arguing with it or trying to make it go away, and then go back to whatever you’ve chosen to do. It’s not necessary to hold a meeting with every thought that comes up, or to do a certain ritual before your life can begin.

old: “What direction would the Leader choose now?”
new: What would the Leader choose to do now?
